channel.title: Controls on P-SSCRM: Proactive Secure Software Supply Chain Risk Management
channel.description: Recent content in Controls on P-SSCRM: Proactive Secure Software Supply Chain Risk Management

item.title: Authentication
item.description: Enable authorization, traceability, and non-repudiation

item.title: Component and container choice
item.description: Make informed third-party component and container choices.

item.title: Criticality analysis
item.description: Identify critical system components and functions by performing a criticality analysis.

item.title: Organizational security requirements
item.description: Organizational security requirements, such as those imposed by standards and regulations, are included in the SDLC.

item.title: Prevent component vetting bypass
item.description: Ensure developers are not bypassing the component vetting process

item.title: Product security requirements
item.description: Identify and document security requirements for organization-developed software, including AI models

item.title: Release policy verification
item.description: Ensure the products, materials, and processes used during the build pipeline adhere to the established product and organizational release policy

item.title: Role-based training
item.description: Provide security training for all personnel involved in software development

item.title: Safely store release artifacts
item.description: Preserve release artifacts to help in the identification and analysis of vulnerabilities discovered after release.

item.title: SBOM consumption
item.description: Utilize SBOM information to react to security incidents and to identify which components need to be updated or patched.

item.title: Security code review
item.description: Detect security vulnerabilities introduced during architecture, design, and source code creation including those injected with malicious intent

item.title: Security design review
item.description: Decrease the number of design flaws and security vulnerabilities introduced during the architecture and design phases.

item.title: Security-related contract terms
item.description: Component, system, AI model, and service acquisition policies include the inclusion of adherence to security policies, security requirements, and secure SDLC practices that are compatible with compliance requirements.

item.title: System monitoring
item.description: Detect runtime product anomalies

item.title: Upper management support
item.description: Upper management understands the business risks of insecure software and supports the resources necessary for secure software development.

item.title: Vulnerability analysis
item.description: Plan the resolution of discovered vulnerabilities

item.title: Automated security scanning tools
item.description: Choose tools to efficiently discover previously-undetected vulnerabilities

item.title: Build process monitoring
item.description: Detect intruders in the build infrastructure

item.title: Contingency training
item.description: Provide training on procedures in the event of a security emergency.

item.title: Dependency update
item.description: Update vulnerable dependency when a fixed version is available

item.title: Emergency artifact fix
item.description: Fix a zero-day vulnerability.

item.title: Environmental separation
item.description: Separate and protect each environment involved in software development (i.e., development, build, test, deployment, model training)

item.title: Risk-based vulnerability remediation
item.description: Remediate vulnerabilities based upon a risk-based prioritization

item.title: Secure coding
item.description: Decrease the number of security vulnerabilities introduced during source code creation.

item.title: Secure SDLC checks
item.description: Criteria throughout the SDLC are used to check the software’s security during development.

item.title: Separation of duties
item.description: Reduce the potential for abuse of authorized privileges and the chance of collusion when acquiring components, systems, and services.

item.title: Software license conflict
item.description: Software licenses that conflict with the organization’s policies are identified.

item.title: Software release integrity
item.description: Provide software acquirers assurance that the software they acquire is legitimate and has not been tampered with.

item.title: Track security risks and decisions
item.description: Record and track the software’s security risk-based exceptions and mitigation plans.

item.title: Trusted repositories
item.description: Obtain candidate packages and containers from trusted ecosystems or rebuild.

item.title: Verify dependencies and environment
item.description: Ensure the build environment’s sources and dependencies come from a secure, trusted source of truth

item.title: Version control
item.description: Prevent unauthorized changes to artifacts, both inadvertent and intentional.

item.title: Automated vulnerability detection
item.description: Detect vulnerabilities before deployment through the use of automated tools to reduce the window of opportunity for attackers.

item.title: Defensive compilation and build
item.description: Reduce vulnerabilities during compilation and build.

item.title: Gather attack trends
item.description: Stay current on attack trends.

item.title: Information disclosure
item.description: Contract language requires that a vendor monitors for information disclosure and notifies the enterprise of information disclosure.

item.title: Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
item.description: Decrease the chances an account will be compromised.

item.title: Produce attestation
item.description: Produce an audit trail for every step in the build process, the integrity/provenance of training data, and evidence of the use of secure software development practices.

item.title: Require signed commits
item.description: Utilize legitimate components and software that has not been tampered with.

item.title: Role-based access control
item.description: Controlling access to resources where permitted actions on resources are identified with roles rather than with individual subject identities; provide traceability between actors and actions

item.title: Roles and responsibilities
item.description: Ownership for security controls throughout the SDLC at the organizational level and at the product team- and operational- level are established and visible.

item.title: Secure-by-default implementation
item.description: Improve the security of software at the time of installation.

item.title: Security metrics
item.description: Provide the basis for the measurement of an effective plan for tracking and realizing software security objectives within an organization.

item.title: Support Upstream Dependencies
item.description: Sustainable open-source software.

item.title: Vulnerability disclosure
item.description: Aid organizations in responding to vulnerabilities to reduce the window of opportunity for attackers

item.title: CI/CD hosting and automation
item.description: Through automated builds, reduce human error and malicious actions and artifacts that cause the output of the build process to contain security vulnerabilities.

item.title: Data-informed product decisions
item.description: Make security decisions on software release based upon criteria for checking the security of the software.

item.title: Deliver provenance
item.description: Enable traceability and reproducibility of the actions performed while writing code, compiling, testing, and deploying software by making transparent the steps that were performed, by whom and in what order.

item.title: Developer SSH key
item.description: Decrease the chances developer account will be compromised.

item.title: Development Environment Scanning Tools
item.description: Detect anomalies in the development infrastructure.

item.title: Executable security testing
item.description: Discover vulnerabilities only detected through executable testing

item.title: Information flow enforcement
item.description: Limit the information flow across trust boundaries to participants in the supply chain

item.title: Security code review policy
item.description: Guidelines on which code should undergo a security-focused manual or automated review are communicated.

item.title: Session audits
item.description: Identify security risks in the supply chain.

item.title: Standard security features
item.description: Reduce introducing new vulnerabilities by reusing standardized and proven security features.

item.title: Vetted third-party component and container repositories
item.description: Engineers can choose from organization-approved components

item.title: Vulnerability eradication
item.description: Proactively eradicate classes of vulnerabilities.

item.title: Asset inventory
item.description: Hardware and software assets are inventoried to enable incident response; system analysis; traceability for critical components; and reliable identification when assets need to be changed or decommissioned.

item.title: Baseline configuration
item.description: Provide the starting point for tracking changes to components, code, and settings throughout the SDLC

item.title: Branch protection
item.description: Provide a formal approval process for code changes to enforce adherence to software development processes and policies before code is introduced into a CI/CD system.

item.title: Deliver SBOM
item.description: By providing SBOM, enable internal and external customers to analyze the contents of the final software package, including the version of the dependencies.

item.title: Establish Response Partnerships
item.description: Develop external incident information sources through collaboration.

item.title: In-house components
item.description: Maintain components built in-house.

item.title: Notification agreement
item.description: Timely notification of security threat and product end-of-life

item.title: Regular third-party compliance
item.description: Identify increased security risk of third-party and open-source components

item.title: Root cause analysis
item.description: Reduce the frequency of vulnerabilities in the future

item.title: Secured orchestration platform
item.description: Ensure each deployed workload meets predetermined security requirements.

item.title: Confirm Integrity of AI model data
item.description: Evaluate AI foundation model, training, and fine-tuning data for potential security impacts.

item.title: Decommission assets
item.description: Prevent security attacks through live end-of-life systems and products

item.title: Monitor changes to configuration settings
item.description: Prevent the tapering of information systems and networks through the monitoring of changes to configuration settings.

item.title: Protection of information at rest
item.description: Protect the confidentiality and integrity of information at rest.

item.title: Reproducible builds
item.description: Provide a mechanism to confirm that no malicious backdoor injections have taken place during the build process.

item.title: Boundary protection
item.description: Monitors and controls communications at the external boundary of the system and at key internal boundaries within the system.

item.title: Build output
item.description: Through protected build environments, reduce human error and malicious actions and artifacts that cause the output of the build process to contain security vulnerabilities.

item.title: Hardened and isolated builds
item.description: Protect the integrity of build output

item.title: Key rotation
item.description: Limit the impact if a key is compromised.

item.title: Ephemeral credentials
item.description: Reduce the number of potential entry points for a hacker, as well as the attack surface.

item.title: Establish a root of trust
item.description: Provide the foundation for secure operations of a computing system
